subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB329 (LANDED 2026-09-05) built this rule's mechanism; kb/Work PB689 gave it a ROW. The row did not exist when PB329 landed -- an interior '## SEQUENTIAL FILES' heading truncated 14.9.51.4's rule block at GR16, so GR17-GR42 were never in the catalog and PB329's implementer had nothing to close. RULE: 'For a line sequential file, if the record area contains one or more characters that are not in the implementor-defined character set defined for a line sequential file, the execution of the WRITE statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status in the write file connector is set to 71.' cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'the execution of the WRITE statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status in the write file connector is set to 71' -> OK 14.9.51.4 23). MECHANISM: LineSequentialCharacterSet is the one executable copy of the Annex A.1 item 115 determination (docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-115: every character at or above U+0020 is a member, the C0 controls below it are not), and SequentialConnector.RecordAreaOutsideLineCharacterSet is the one call shape. BOTH write entry points consult it -- Write and WriteAdvancing -- ahead of every shape branch, because the rule is organization-scoped rather than shape-scoped, and ahead of any stream traffic because 9.1.13.10 item 1 requires the record area and the medium to be left unchanged. (There were THREE until kb/Work PB712, 2026-09-06, deleted the third arm, the BEFORE-AND-AFTER write: 14.9.51.2 Format 1 prints ONE ADVANCING operand, so the COBOL-2023 BEFORE AFTER pair is a placement and reaches WriteAdvancing like every other print-control write. The arm count fell; the coverage did not.) The test is CHARACTER-wise, not byte-wise: a national record area is walked two bytes at a time as UTF-16BE, so N"CD"'s 00 43 00 44 is two members and not two control characters. MEASURED on the built cobol.exe before PB329 landed: a line sequential WRITE of a record holding 0x00 reported STATUS=00 and left the byte on the medium; after, STATUS=71 and the file is 0 bytes. Goldens walk 09 (READ, 14.9.30.4 GR16), 71 (WRITE, THIS rule), 71 (REWRITE, 14.9.35.4 GR17d), the unchanged medium, and the set boundary (0x7F -> ordinal 128, 0xFF -> ordinal 256 are members) at 2023, the one edition the LINE SEQUENTIAL organization exists in. kb/Work PB688 (2026-09-05): ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL is a COBOL-2023 INTRODUCTION - the Foreword's list of the main changes this third edition makes over ISO/IEC 1989:2014 names "Line Sequential file organization", and 9.1.6 / 9.1.7.1 still name exactly three organizations with 9.1.7.2 splitting the sequential one into its record- and line-delimited types. The organization therefore does not exist below 2023 (the pass now rejects it with COBOL0900, registry row file-organization-line-sequential-2023), the 2002 and 2014 copies of the golden were deleted as programs no edition below 2023 can express, and this row's editions are 2023 alone. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/SequentialConnector.cs#WriteBeforeAndAfter (WriteBeforeAndAfter was deleted: BEFORE AFTER ADVANCING is one placement and reaches WriteAdvancing (kb/Work PB712, 30496b642))
